title: Rotational Kinematics
short: ω = ω₀ + αt and θ = ω₀t + ½αt² mirror the straight-line equations.
trouble: Students put a distance where the angle belongs, or mix revolutions with radians.

blocks.html: When the angular acceleration is constant, turning follows the same equations as motion with constant acceleration, with each letter swapped for its rotational twin.

The straight-line equations came from two facts: velocity changes at a steady rate, and displacement is the area under the velocity–time graph. Both facts hold for turning. If $\alpha$ is constant, $\omega$ rises along a straight line in time, and the angle turned is the area under the $\omega$–$t$ graph. So the algebra is identical; only the names change.

With constant $\alpha$: $\role{angvel}{\omega} = \role[initial angular velocity]{angvel}{\omega_0} + \role{angacc}{\alpha}\role{time}{t}$, $\role[angle turned]{angle}{\Delta\theta} = \role[initial angular velocity]{angvel}{\omega_0} \role{time}{t} + \tfrac{1}{2}\role{angacc}{\alpha} \role{time}{t}^2$ and $\role{angvel}{\omega}^2 = \role[initial angular velocity]{angvel}{\omega_0}^2 + 2\role{angacc}{\alpha}\role[angle turned]{angle}{\Delta\theta}$. Angles in radians, $\omega$ in rad/s, $\alpha$ in rad/s². Divide radians by $2\pi$ to count revolutions.

blocks.name: ph-graph

opts.task: The slope of the $\omega$–$t$ graph is $\alpha$; the shaded area is the angle turned.

blocks.cap: A wheel speeding up from $2$ to $10\ \text{rad/s}$ in $4\ \text{s}$: slope $\alpha = 2\ \text{rad/s}^2$, area $\Delta\theta = 24\ \text{rad}$.

blocks.title: Speeding up
blocks.q: A wheel turning at $2.0\ \text{rad/s}$ speeds up at $2.0\ \text{rad/s}^2$ for $4.0\ \text{s}$. Find its final $\omega$ and the angle it turns.

blocks.title: Coasting to a stop
blocks.q: A grinding wheel at $1800$ rpm is switched off and slows at $5.0\ \text{rad/s}^2$. How many revolutions does it make before stopping?
steps: No time is given, so use $0 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\Delta\theta$: $\Delta\theta = \dfrac{188.5^2}{2(5.0)} = 3553\ \text{rad}$.

blocks.title: How long it takes
blocks.q: For the same grinding wheel, how long does it take to stop?
steps: Check with the average angular velocity: $\Delta\theta = \tfrac{1}{2}(188.5 + 0)(37.7) = 3553\ \text{rad}$, the same angle as before.

blocks.html: Putting a distance where the angle belongs, or mixing revolutions with radians. In $\Delta\theta = \omega_0 t + \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha t^2$ every term must be in radians, so $\omega$ must be in rad/s, not rpm. A distance (meters) never goes in for $\theta$; if you want the distance a point travels, find $\theta$ first and then use $s = r\theta$. Check the units: rad/s times s gives rad.
